items.title: Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDA. Why Apple, Broadcom, and Anthropic Could Be Under Pressure
items.teaser: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) sent stocks sharply higher on Monday morning. NVIDIA shares opened up 34% at about $170, restoring more than $1 trillion of value to shareholders. The NASDAQ rose about 6.75% and the S&P 500 about 4.6%, erasing much of Friday's sell-off. Bleeker focuses on stocks lagging a market where nearly everything is up. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) gained only about 1.7%, and he says a rotation back into AI-adjacent names could pull capital out of the safe-haven stock. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) rose about 6% at the open, trailing the NASDAQ and semiconductor indexes. It fell about 12% Friday on reports that Google was cutting some of its TPU allocation. Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) also rose 6%, but its shares have been under pressure since Thursday's IPO, and NVIDIA's backing of open-weight models is a competitive threat. CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 5% at the open, partly on its $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS). Bleeker notes that money that moved into cybersecurity as semiconductors sold off could rotate back. He says to watch for competitive pressure on these names in the coming weeks.
